name: update, scripting, monochrome
plain: Screen refresh type, whether JS is enabled, and monochrome depth.
meaning: update is none for e-ink or print; scripting reports enabled or none; monochrome is 0 on color screens. Mostly identifies e-readers and print contexts.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

fields.name: update, scripting, monochrome
fields.range: update: none, slow, fast; scripting: none, initial-only, enabled; monochrome: 0 to 16

limits.headline: Can tell how your screen refreshes, if scripting is on, and if it is monochrome
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads.
can: Check whether the screen updates slowly, like an e-ink reader
Check whether the screen is monochrome
cannot: See anything else about your screen

story.what_it_is: Reports how your screen refreshes, whether scripts run, and whether the display is black and white.

marketing.name: update media feature
marketing.pitch: Documents how a page can tell whether the screen refreshes quickly, slowly or never, like e ink or print.

story.for_you: You never see the reading. On a normal screen the answers are always the same. They only differ for e ink readers, printers or very basic setups.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to serve printable or slow screen layouts. Because almost everyone gives the same answer, the values are weak for tracking, but odd answers can reveal unusual or automated browsers.

use_cases.example: A reading site serves a plain layout with no animation on an e ink tablet.
A browser game turns off fast animation if it runs on a very slow refresh screen.
A fraud check sees a browser that says scripts are off while running scripts, a sign of a masked or automated tool.
A store gives a clean black and white print page for receipts and coupons.
A learning site makes a printable worksheet in grayscale.
A team checks how many visitors have a non standard display before dropping old support.

technical_bounds: scripting: none only visible to CSS, since JS reports enabled

legit_uses: Respect OS theme and accessibility needs
abuse: Infer disability or setting for fingerprinting
